The literature this site and the benchmark protocol rely on, with a line on why each matters.

# The model

- **Moore, R. J. (2007).** The PDM rainfall-runoff model. *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*,
  11, 483–499. [doi:10.5194/hess-11-483-2007](https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-11-483-2007).
  The definitive description of the model, its variants and its updating methods. pdmS7 follows
  its equations and numbering; see [Model equations](model-equations.html).

# Testing models

- **Klemeš, V. (1986).** Operational testing of hydrological simulation models. *Hydrological
  Sciences Journal*, 31, 13–24. The split-sample hierarchy behind calibration, validation and test
  windows, and the stronger differential test for changing conditions.
- **Seibert, J., Vis, M. J. P., Lewis, E. and van Meerveld, H. J. (2018).** Upper and lower
  benchmarks in hydrological modelling. *Hydrological Processes*, 32, 1120–1125. Why a score needs
  a floor to mean anything; the source of the protocol's day-of-year lower benchmark.
- **Andréassian, V. et al. (2009).** Crash tests for a standardized evaluation of hydrological
  models. *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*, 13, 1757–1764. Testing models where they are
  most likely to fail.

# Scores

- **Gupta, H. V., Kling, H., Yilmaz, K. K. and Martinez, G. F. (2009).** Decomposition of the
  mean squared error and NSE performance criteria. *Journal of Hydrology*, 377, 80–91. The origin
  of KGE and its three terms.
- **Yilmaz, K. K., Gupta, H. V. and Wagener, T. (2008).** A process-based diagnostic evaluation of
  a hydrologic model. *Water Resources Research*, 44, W09417. The flow-duration curve signatures
  reported by `pdm_scorecard()`.
- **Knoben, W. J. M., Freer, J. E. and Woods, R. A. (2019).** Technical note: Inherent benchmark
  or not? Comparing Nash–Sutcliffe and Kling–Gupta efficiency scores. *Hydrology and Earth System
  Sciences*, 23, 4323–4331. Why NSE and KGE values cannot be compared with each other directly.
- **Clark, M. P. et al. (2021).** The abuse of popular performance metrics in hydrologic modeling.
  *Water Resources Research*, 57, e2020WR029001. How sampling uncertainty in a score can swamp
  the difference between models; why the protocol reports distributions and paired differences.

# Machine learning in hydrology

- **Kratzert, F. et al. (2019).** Towards learning universal, regional, and local hydrological
  behaviors via machine learning applied to large-sample datasets. *Hydrology and Earth System
  Sciences*, 23, 5089–5110. The regional LSTM that set the modern benchmark.
- **Gauch, M. et al. (2021).** Rainfall–runoff prediction at multiple timescales with a single
  Long Short-Term Memory network. *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*, 25, 2045–2062. LSTMs at
  sub-daily steps, relevant to phase 2 of the protocol.
- **Lees, T. et al. (2021).** Benchmarking data-driven rainfall–runoff models in Great Britain: a
  comparison of long short-term memory (LSTM)-based models with four lumped conceptual models.
  *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*, 25, 5517–5534. The published comparison that phase 1 of
  the protocol copies.
- **Mai, J. et al. (2022).** The Great Lakes Runoff Intercomparison Project Phase 4: the Great
  Lakes (GRIP-GL). *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*, 26, 3537–3572. A model intercomparison
  run to a fixed protocol, with conceptual and machine-learning models together.
- **Nearing, G. S. et al. (2021).** What role does hydrological science play in the age of
  machine learning? *Water Resources Research*, 57, e2020WR028091. The wider argument the
  comparison speaks to.

# Data

- **Coxon, G. et al. (2020).** CAMELS-GB: hydrometeorological time series and landscape
  attributes for 671 catchments in Great Britain. *Earth System Science Data*, 12, 2459–2483.
  The dataset for phase 1 of the protocol.

# Forecasting

- **Pappenberger, F. et al. (2015).** How do I know if my forecasts are better? Using benchmarks
  in hydrological ensemble prediction. *Journal of Hydrology*, 522, 697–713. Persistence and
  climatology as baselines for forecast skill, as used by `hindcast_scores()`.

# Related packages

- [reach.io](https://github.com/JonPayneEA/reach.io): hydrometric data from the EA Hydrology
  API, with Bronze and Silver stores, quality flags and ratings. See [Preparing your
  data](data-preparation.html).
- [reach.postproc](https://github.com/JonPayneEA/reach.postproc): AR and ARMA post-processing for
  flood forecasts, with the Environment Agency parameter assessment. See [AR and ARMA error
  correction, explained](ar-error-correction.html).
